# Report: H. G. Wells, *The Time Machine*, opening (chs. I–V)

## 1. The question, frozen

The passage answers several questions (what the future holds; how far the race declines). The title and the opening make one central: **Can a body be carried through Time as through Space, and what shows that it can?** Range: this room, this evening, the model on the octagonal table, and the unfinished big machine in the laboratory. What is asked: what produces movement in Time — and why is it said that we cannot move in Time now? The first is forward ("what produces it"), the second is the Medical Man's block ("why can it not happen"). I am judging the explanation the Time Traveller puts in the room, not the novel's quality.

## 2. The parts, in his words

A mathematical line and plane have "no real existence"; a real body must have extension in Length, Breadth, Thickness **and Duration**; "there is no difference between Time and any of the three dimensions of Space except that our consciousness moves along it"; "a natural infirmity of the flesh" hides this; the barometer record traces a line "along the Time-Dimension"; portraits at eight, fifteen, twenty-three are "sections" of "a fixed and unalterable thing"; "gravitation limits us" up and down, but balloons; the model vanishes; the Psychologist's "diluted presentation"; the traveller's return — dust, a half-healed cut, bare feet, hunger.

## 3. Part by part

| Part | Mark |
|---|---|
| "a mathematical line... has no real existence" | **borrowed** — rests on the convention that ideal figures are abstractions; not tested here |
| "extension in four directions... Duration" | **borrowed** — the four-dimensional geometry of his day (Newcomb is named in the text) |
| "no difference... except that our consciousness moves along it" | **held if** — held only by the job "explain why Time has always been thought different." It does that job by relocating the difference to the observer; that relocation is asserted |
| "a natural infirmity of the flesh" | **held if** — a bin for why we do not see it. Its gauge is the Psychologist's spinning wheel and flying bullet |
| the barometer trace | **loose** — any record plotted against time draws the same line; a table of readings would do. What is held is that records *can be drawn* with a time axis, which is a fact about drawing |
| portraits as "sections" | **loose** — the ages eight, fifteen, twenty-three are free; any successive snapshots would serve |
| "...a fixed and unalterable thing" | **held if** — the block universe. Asserted here, and catchable elsewhere |
| "Gravitation limits us... balloons" | **built** — says something definite about the *shape* of the limit: it is empirical and a mechanism can lift it |
| the model vanishes | **held if** — held by the job "show it moved in Time and not in Space." The trick rival is answered by the narrator's assertion, not by a test |
| "diluted presentation" | **loose** — a patch made after the objection. Any fast-moving thing is invisible to us, so it can be swapped freely — and it hands the trick hypothesis a way to make things vanish |
| the return: dust, cut chin, feet, hunger | **held** — a different kind of check from the vanishing. A conjuror cannot supply the wear on the man |

## 4. Whole-explanation checks

**Flip.** Had the model *not* vanished, the same argument would have been offered as proof that Time is a dimension we cannot move in. The "no difference" clause is doing the work; it would fit either outcome. That is a loose joint.

**Direction.** The barometer line and the portraits run backwards — from a drawn appearance to a cause. They are answers to "what can we tell from what we see," presented as "what produces it." A line on paper is changed by redrawing it, not by changing Time. This is the method's measurement trap: the part moves when only its reading is changed.

**The answer in the starting points.** "Time is only a kind of Space" already contains "we may travel in Time." The argument gives the conclusion back in a new suit.

**Jobs: where they came from.** The sharpest jobs are **given** by the room — the Medical Man's "why can we not move in Time?", his "why has it always been thought different?", the Psychologist's "why do we not see it?" That is a strength: the jobs were not written to fit the parts. The block-universe job ("what does this imply for the future?") is **added** by the Time Traveller, and the part held by it is only *held if*.

**Pairs that pull.** "Diluted presentation" against the demonstration. To explain why we don't see it, he gives a reason things disappear from view — which also gives a reason the vanishing need not mean time travel. Tightening one loosens the other. Where the line is drawn is exactly the disputed point, and what would show it wrongly drawn is a second vanishing under conditions where dilution is ruled out.

**Catch-all and gauge.** "Infirmity of the flesh" is a bin; it is allowed because the spinning-wheel analogy can be checked — tell us what fraction of our own speed it moves at, and something should look odd.

**Rivals.** Conjuring trick; hallucination; the earlier Christmas ghost. What tells them apart: a second kind of evidence. The document supplies it — the man comes back starved, cut, limping, with his socks in rags. That is the document's own best move, and it is not the same check repeated.

**What the change list leaves out.** Nothing is claimed about being seen while travelling, about arriving at a chosen date, or about what happens to the traveller's nerves beyond sensation. Those are left out silently.

**Where the parts came from.** Mostly **borrowed** (four-dimensional geometry) and **asserted** (the block universe, the "no difference" clause). One is **seen** (the vanishing, under conditions the narrator describes). One is **fitted** (the dilution patch). None is shown to be built and then criticised.

## 5. What would make it harder to vary

Two moves. First, replace the barometer with a change that should matter and one that should not: the machine at speed should read differently, and repainting the machine should not. Second, keep the return as the load-bearing test and face the trick rival directly — the traveller should come back with something a trick cannot produce, and say beforehand what.

## 6. What this does not show

Passing would not make time travel true, and the loose parts may be true. This test finds what holds a part in place; it does not rank the novel, and it does not judge taste.

## 7. One next step

Have the Time Traveller name, before he goes, one thing he expects to find and one he does not — then see whether the return supplies it.
